findings: Source Theorem 2.1 (PDF p. 4) and Appendix A.1 (PDF p. 19) were checked visually and in full extracted text. The proof claims per-coordinate score distortion epsilon preserves labels when the original margin is only epsilon; this is false because the margin may change by 2epsilon.

The local item repairs the theorem: coordinatewise score distortion epsilon yields empirical compressed zero-one loss at most the original empirical 2epsilon-margin loss. A confidence-1-delta Hoeffding/union bound over at most r^q codes yields sqrt((q log r+log(1/delta))/(2m)).
The guarantee is for the compressed classifier. The original network needs a separate all-domain loss-preservation argument; specialized neural construction remains unaudited.

findings: The convex stability result uses convex, beta-smooth, L-Lipschitz losses and alpha_t<=2/beta; the nonconvex theorem separately uses losses in [0,1], L-Lipschitz/beta-smoothness, and nonincreasing alpha_t<=c/t.
The nonconvex displayed formula has denominator n-1, so the pair explicitly requires n>=2. It is an expected generalization gap under the source SGM sample-selection rules, not a universal SGD claim.
The couple-neighboring-samples proof uses the same selection sequence and a different recursion in convex/nonconvex regimes.
